sources.fact: LBBD83/HQ Town Quay Wharf is 0.54ha, deliverable=yes, 147 net dwellings and planning-permission-status permissioned.
HQ has point POINT (0.074111 51.534727) and blank geometry; point is not exact application/title polygon.
Brownfield entry carries an official planning-history link but the exact final planning application reference was not independently resolved in this wave.
Be First describes Town Quay Wharf as 147 homes in total, comprising 62 council/affordable homes and 85 private-sale homes.
Be First confirms 147 apartments and acquisition of 62 affordable units for the Council.
The 62 affordable units were described as 29 London Affordable Rent and 33 shared ownership.
Cabinet approved purchase of 62 affordable homes and land-transfer/borrowing arrangements supporting the Town Quay redevelopment.
Cabinet decision records purchase price £14,635,162 for 62 affordable homes; this transaction figure is not a parcel market valuation.
December 2024 Cabinet minutes record disposal/lease arrangements for Town Quay Wharf new-build homes following practical completion over coming months.
December 2024 decision expected Town Quay Wharf completion in January 2025 and approved long-lease/loan arrangements; delivery evidence does not establish title polygon relation.
Adopted Local Plan allocation HQ Town Quay Wharf has indicative net minimum capacity 147, matching the Brownfield and Be First total.
LBBD Brownfield Register inclusion is not itself planning permission; HQ permission status is retained because the authoritative register explicitly marks it permissioned.

examples.result: HQ total of 147 homes is reconciled across Brownfield, Local Plan and Be First delivery sources.
62 affordable + 85 private = 147 total is preserved as tenure/delivery composition, not a new capacity estimate.
Cabinet purchase price is not converted into whole-site market value or viability score.
December 2024/January 2025 completion evidence is delivery evidence, not exact HMLR title binding.
Brownfield point is not treated as the Town Quay Wharf legal parcel.
Exact final planning-application reference remains unresolved in this wave and is not guessed from older Quayside House cases.
Permissioned status is retained from the authoritative Brownfield record without manufacturing missing red-line geometry.
Promotion remains zero until exact title/site relation and current statutory overlays are executed.
